questionText: Find the equation of the tangent to the curve $y = x^2 - 3x$ at the point where $x = 2$.
markingScheme:
Find $y$-coordinate at $x = 2$: $y = 4 - 6 = -2$ **(1 mark)**
Differentiate: $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 2x - 3$ **(1 mark)**
Substitute $x = 2$ to find slope $= 1$ **(1 mark)**
Apply point-slope form **(1 mark)**
Final answer $y = x - 4$ **(1 mark)**

solutionSteps.step: Find the point on the curve
solutionSteps.explanation: At $x = 2$: $y = 2^2 - 3(2) = 4 - 6 = -2$. The point of tangency is $(2,\,-2)$.
Using point-slope form $y - y_1 = m(x - x_1)$: $y - (-2) = 1(x - 2)$, which simplifies to $y = x - 4$.
